qna.question: What does the G-Sec Yield Spread (1-Year & 3-Year) data represent?
qna.answer: The G-Sec Yield Spread (1-Year & 3-Year) data represents the difference between short-term (1-year) and medium term maturities (3-year) government securities (G-Sec) yield.^The spread is calculated by subtracting the 1-year G-Sec yield from the 3-year G-Sec yield.

qna.question: What is the significance of the G-Sec Yield Spread (1-Year & 3-Year) data?
How to interpret the G-Sec Yield Spread (1-Year & 3-Year) data?
qna.answer: A wider spread might indicate expectations of higher interest rates in the medium term, while a narrower spread could suggest relatively higher interest rates in the near-term.^A widening spread may suggest bullish sentiment towards the economy in the medium term, while a narrowing spread might indicate concerns about short-term economic prospects.^A widening spread might suggest higher anticipated inflation, impacting long-term interest rates.^The negative spread between shorter and medium term G-Sec yields, indicates an inversion of the yield curve and is often viewed as a predictor of sharp slowdown in economic growth or an impending recession.^A negative spread  suggests higher perceived risk in the near-term than in the medium term. Investors are willing to accept lower yields on 3 year securities for the perceived safety they offer compared to riskier 1-year securities, especially in times of economic uncertainty.
